description: Robustness of the memory router against untrusted / malformed LLM output: reasoning-leak, CJK-leak, empty/invalid entries, malformed JSON, and null/non-array shapes. Links to 12 §4 (recalled memory is untrusted). Prompt-injection round-trip-inert, delimiter-collision escaping and recall caps (14 §6) are v2-spec requirements absent in v1 and registered as GAP-05. T14-08 closed the formatter-level slice (`adversarial.recall.*`: additionalContext sanitization/escaping/caps, spec 11 §5/12 §4) with real unit tests in `crates/memory/src/recall/format.rs`. T16-04 closes GAP-05's remaining end-to-end slice (stored memory -> real op engine -> wired recall -> inert output, `adversarial.recall.end-to-end-*`) plus the adjacent corpus the card also names -- malicious indexed code (`adversarial.code.*`), source secrets and symlink escapes through the real scan/reconcile/build pipeline (`adversarial.index.*`), and hook-captured secrets never touching disk (`adversarial.hook.*`) -- each case's `provenance.ref` names the real Rust test that asserts it. This family has no generic JSON-loading runner (unlike `parser`/`fault`); every case here, T14-08's and T16-04's alike, is a hand-written test that documents its fixture-id correspondence in `provenance`/comments rather than loading this file at runtime.
